title: Debouncing & Throttling
definition: Debouncing and Throttling are two techniques to control how many times we allow a function to be executed over time. Debouncing delays the function execution until a certain amount of time has passed since the last time it was called. Throttling limits the function execution to at most once every specified time interval.
simpleExplanation:
Imagine an elevator with doors about to close. 
**Debounce**: Every time a new person arrives, you reset the timer. The elevator won't leave until 5 seconds pass with NO new people arriving.
**Throttle**: The elevator leaves strictly every 10 minutes. Doesn't matter how many people arrive or mash the button, it only departs on that exact schedule.
realWorldExample: Debounce is used for Search Bars: wait until the user stops typing for 300ms before making an API call. Throttle is used for Scroll events: if a user scrolls rapidly, you only want to check the scroll position once every 100ms so the browser doesn't freeze.

answers.question: What is the main difference?
answers.answer: Debounce groups multiple sequential calls into a single execution at the very end of the burst. Throttle guarantees execution at a regular, steady interval regardless of how many times it was called.

answers.question: In a search bar, which technique would you use and why?
answers.answer: Debounce. If a user types 'hello', that's 5 keystrokes. You don't want to make 5 API calls. You want to wait until they finish typing the word (e.g., 300ms of silence) and then make exactly 1 API call for 'hello'.

answers.question: If you set a debounce delay to 0ms, does it execute synchronously?
answers.answer: No. `setTimeout` with 0ms still pushes the callback to the Task Queue, so it will execute asynchronously after the current synchronous Call Stack is clear.
